Q1.Problem to demonstrate that the population regression line is fixed, but least square regression line varies.





```{r}
#Step 1: Take 200 equidistant points in the range [5:10]
x=seq(5,10,length.out=200)
y=2+3*x
plot(x,y,type='l',lwd=3,main="Plot of the PRF Y=2+3x")
#Step 2: Generate xi from U(5,10) and ei from N(0,16)
n=50
set.seed(123)
xi=runif(n,5,10)
ei=rnorm(n,0,4)
#SRF y=2+3x+e
yi=2+3*xi+ei
#Overlaying the the points on the PRF
plot(x,y,type='l',lwd=4,main="Plot of the PRF Y=2+3x and the Sample points")
points(xi,yi)
#Step 3: Least Square Regression line
model1=lm(yi~xi)
summary(model1)
y.hat=-0.09639+3.30540*xi  #SRF
#Overlaying the PRF and SRF
plot(x,y,type='l',lwd=2,main="Plot of the PRF and the SRF")
lines(xi,y.hat,type='l',col="blue",lty="dotted")
legend("topleft",col=c("black","blue"),lwd=c(2,1),legend=c("PRF","SRF"),
       lty=c("solid","dotted"))
#Step 4: Repeat step 2 and 3 for 5 times.
set.seed(123)
x1=runif(n,5,10)
e1=rnorm(n,0,4)
y1=2+3*x1+e1
fit1=lm(y1~x1)
summary(fit1)


x2=runif(n,5,10)
e2=rnorm(n,0,4)
y2=2+3*x2+e2
fit2=lm(y2~x2)

x3=runif(n,5,10)
e3=rnorm(n,0,4)
y3=2+3*x3+e3
fit3=lm(y3~x3)

x4=runif(n,5,10)
e4=rnorm(n,0,4)
y4=2+3*x4+e4
fit4=lm(y4~x4)

x5=runif(n,5,10)
e5=rnorm(n,0,4)
y5=2+3*x5+e5
fit5=lm(y5~x5)

#Data frame containing the five models' coefficients
coeff=data.frame(coef(fit1),
                 coef(fit2),
                 coef(fit3),
                 coef(fit4),
                 coef(fit5))
coeff

#Plot of the PRF and the Five SRFs

plot(x,y,type='l',lwd=3,main="Plot of the PRF and the Five SRFs")
lines(x1,predict(fit1),type='l',col="yellow")
lines(x2,predict(fit2),type='l',col="brown")
lines(x3,predict(fit3),type='l',col="cyan")
lines(x4,predict(fit4),type='l',col="darkblue")
lines(x5,predict(fit5),type='l',col="orange")
legend("topleft",legend=c("PRF","Model 1","Model 2","Model 3",
                          "Model 4","Model 5"),
       col=c("black","yellow","brown","cyan","darkblue","orange"),
       lwd=c(3,1,1,1,1,1))

```

Q2.Problem to demonstrate that βˆ0 and βˆ minimises RSS

```{r}

#step 1: Generate xi~U(5,10) of size 50, and ei~N(0,1)
#y=2+3x+e
n=50
set.seed(123)
x=runif(n,5,10)
x_mean=x-mean(x)
e=rnorm(n)
y=2+3*xm+e
fit=lm(y~x_mean)
summary(fit)
beta0=2.0562
beta=3.0764
#Creating the beta and beta0 grid values
beta0.grid=seq(-1,1,length.out=101)+beta0
beta.grid=seq(-1,1,length.out=101)+beta
#Computing RSS
RSS=c()
for(i in 1:length(beta.grid))
{
  RSS[i]=sum((y-beta0.grid[i]-beta.grid[i]*xm)^2)
}
RSS
df=data.frame(beta0.grid,beta.grid,RSS)
df
df[which.min(RSS),]



```

Thus we can verify the LSE minimises the RSS


Q3.Problem to demonstrate that least square estimators are unbiased

```{r}
#Step 1: Generate xi~U(5,10) of size 50, and ei~N(0,1)
n=50
set.seed(123)
x=runif(n,0,1)
e=rnorm(n)
y=2+3*x+e
#Step 2: obtain LSE
fit=lm(y~x)
summary(fit)
beta_0_hat=1.8576
beta_hat=3.3817
#Repeat R=1000 times
set.seed(123)
R=10000
beta_0=numeric(R)
beta=numeric(R)
n=50
for(i in 1:R) {
  x=runif(n,0,1)              
  e=rnorm(n,0,1)            
  y=2+3*x+e      
  fit=lm(y~x)
  beta_0[i]=coef(fit)[1]    
  beta[i]=coef(fit)[2]      
}
mean(beta_0)
mean(beta)

#the long run means of beta_0_hat and beta_hat converges to true beta and beta0

var(beta_0)
var(beta)

#variance approaches 0 as R goes up. Hence LSE is consistent.
```


QProblem 4: Comparing several simple linear regressions

```{r}

rm(list=ls())
library(MASS)
attach(Boston)
y=medv
x1=lstat
x2=crim
x3=nox
x4=black

#(a)
fit1=lm(medv~lstat)
fit2=lm(medv~crim)
fit3=lm(medv~nox)
fit4=lm(medv~black)
install.packages("stargazer")
library(stargazer)
stargazer(fit1,fit2,fit3,fit4,type="text",out="f.txt")


```


```{r}
# Simplified code focusing only on parts (b) and (c)

# Load data
library(MASS)
data(Boston)

# Run the four regressions
models <- list()
r_squared <- numeric(4)
predictors <- c("crim", "nox", "black", "lstat")

for (i in 1:4) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste("medv ~", predictors[i]))
  models[[i]] <- lm(formula, data = Boston)
  r_squared[i] <- summary(models[[i]])$r.squared
}

# (b): Find best model
best_predictor <- predictors[which.max(r_squared)]
best_r2 <- max(r_squared)

cat("PART (b) ANSWER:\n")
cat("Best predictor:", best_predictor, "\n")
cat("R-squared:", round(best_r2, 4), "\n")
cat("This explains", round(best_r2 * 100, 1), "% of variance in home values.\n\n")

# (c): Compare predictors
cat("PART (c) ANSWER:\n")
cat("Comparison of predictors:\n")
cat("-----------------------\n")

for (i in 1:4) {
  coef_val <- coef(models[[i]])[2]
  p_val <- coef(summary(models[[i]]))[2, 4]
  
  cat(predictors[i], ":\n")
  cat("  Coefficient:", round(coef_val, 4), "\n")
  cat("  R-squared:", round(r_squared[i], 4), "\n")
  cat("  Significance:", ifelse(p_val < 0.05, "Significant", "Not significant"), "\n")
  
  if (coef_val < 0) {
    cat("  As", predictors[i], "increases, home values decrease.\n")
  } else {
    cat("  As", predictors[i], "increases, home values increase.\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
}


ranking <- order(r_squared, decreasing = TRUE)
cat("Ranking from most to least useful:\n")
for (i in 1:4) {
  cat(i, ". ", predictors[ranking[i]], " (R² = ", round(r_squared[ranking[i]], 3), ")\n", sep = "")
}
```
